evidence: books/payload-arena-extent.lisp:578-583: `(defun fn-arx-stage-grow (h fn-arena$x) ... (if (< h (fn-arena$x-stage-length fn-arena$x)) fn-arena$x (resize-fn-arena$x-stage (max 64 (* 2 h)) fn-arena$x)))`, called from fn-arena$x-seal-buffer (:611-621) with `h (fn-arena$x-count fn-arena$x)`. The slots are child stobjs (`(fn-arena$x-stage :type (array fn-arena-page (0)) :resizable t)`, :57). fn-arena$x-release (:687-700) only resizes a slot's bytes to 0 and never shrinks the array.
fix: Key the stage by a small slot pool instead of by handle. For example, keep a map from handle to stage slot in EXT (`(:staged slot)`), recycle slots on release, and size the pool to the batches in flight. Alternatively grow the stage to (1+ h) relative to a base offset of the first staged handle.
reviewer: fn-arena$x-seal-buffer (payload-arena-extent.lisp:611-621) stages the handle h = fn-arena$x-count and calls fn-arx-stage-grow, which resizes the stage to max(64, 2h) slots (:578-583). Each slot is a child fn-arena-page stobj (:57). Extent seals never grow the stage, so after a replay of N articles the first POST allocates about 2N page stobjs. fn-arena$x-release (:687-700) only empties a page's bytes and never shrinks the array. The header's claim at :26-27 ('staged octets bounded by the batches not yet durable') is true of the octets but not of the slot array, which grows with the store.
scenario: An open replays 10M articles as extent seals (fn-arena$x-seal-extent never grows the stage). The first served POST stages handle 10,000,000, which resizes the stage to 20,000,000 slots, each a fresh fn-arena-page stobj with its own empty byte array. That is hundreds of MB to over 1 GB of heap for slots that will never hold a payload, since only handles staged in an in-flight batch ever use one. The cost grows with the store, not with the batches in flight, which contradicts the header's claim that 'the staged octets are bounded by the batches not yet durable'.
title: The arena's stage array is indexed by global handle, so the first POST after a large replay allocates 2x(handle count) empty page stobjs that are never shrunk
